title: Query Model Updates inside Command Model (Unnecessary DB Joins)
damaged_code:
```ruby
def update_cargo_status(cargo_id, status)
    cargo = CargoRepository.find(cargo_id) # Loads full aggregate
    cargo.status = status                  # Saves back to DB
end
```
pattern: Loading a highly complex, multi-entity domain aggregate merely to perform a simple status update or field write.
why_bad: Forces expensive multi-table joins and object instantiation overhead just to execute a trivial state mutation that only requires a target ID reference.
detection: Commands that load full entity state or join parent-child tables before modifying a minor attribute.
counterexample: The database is a pure object-oriented database where memory object traversal is exceptionally fast. `Contextual`.
fix: Decouple reads and writes using CQRS (Command-Query Responsibility Segregation), updating target fields by direct ID reference.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 10, CQRS (p. 503) and *Domain Modeling Made Functional*, Chapter 10 (p. 470).
